messages:
maria (ml-infra): heads-up — starting a canary rollout for the preseeder warmers on the canary fleet. goal: improve KV prefix hit rate for common prompts during scale and deploy events. will run at 10% traffic for 24h. :rocket:
cesar (runtime): nice. what keying are you using for the preseed requests? last time we saw collisions when we only used raw prompt text.
maria (ml-infra): using shard-aware keying: `hash(normalize(prompt)) + ':' + model_variant + ':' + shard_id`. normalize = lowercase + strip whitespace + truncate to 1024 chars. avoids cross-shard duplicates.
kevin (sre): adding autoscaler hooks — can we trigger warmers on scale-up events? otherwise newly provisioned replicas are cold and tail latency spikes.
cesar (runtime): yes, autoscaler will emit `scale_event` webhook. plan: `on_scale_up` -> spawn per-shard preseed job limited to top-k prefixes. avoid saturating GPU by rate-limiting requests to 20 qps per replica.
anh (prod-eng): curious about synthetic traffic vs real prefix lists. are we using sampled production prefixes or synthetic templates?
maria (ml-infra): sampled top-5k prefixes from last 7 days, plus templated fallbacks for long-form completions. synthetic template set used only for low-frequency routes.
cesar (runtime): FYI we profiled the preseeder path with kernel v2 and saw a regression: kernel selection changed scheduling which increased KV lookup latency under contention. observed ~12% p95 increase for preseed RPCs.
kevin (sre): did that correlate with new batching heuristics rollout? we rolled batching tweaks last week.
cesar (runtime): partially. batching change + cuda-kernel-v2 scheduling produced higher lock contention in the KV layer during heavy warmers. I attached sample flame output to the thread (pasted snippet):
```
KV::lookup_hot_trie  45%  (contention on mutex)
cuda_kernel_dispatch  30%
batch_scheduler_poll  15%
other 10%
```
maria (ml-infra): thanks — sounds like preseeder should run with limited concurrency and prefer streaming warmers that use smaller batch sizes. current canary config: concurrency=8, batch_target=64. propose concurrency=2, batch_target=8 for warmers.
anh (prod-eng): agree. also propose adding a deploy-time preseed hook: when a new model variant is deployed, run a deploy-seed job that warms only the canary replicas with that model_variant keys. will gate rollout until hit-rate > 60% on canary.
cesar (runtime): implementation note: add `model_variant` tag to cache key (already done) and add `deploy-seed` endpoint: `POST /internal/warmers/seed {variant, prefixes[], mode: "deploy"}`. warmbot can call that on successful canary deploy.
warmbot: deploy succeeded for `redwood-opt-8q-v1` on canary-3. triggered `deploy-seed` for 2,000 top prefixes.
kevin (sre): post-rollout observation plan: monitor KV hit-rate, preseed RPC latency, and tail latency on user requests. set alert: if p95 user latency increases >5% for 30m, rollback warmers.
maria (ml-infra): running quick perf test: baseline hit-rate (no presseed) = 18%; initial canary (old config) = 37%; new limited-concurrency warmers = 54% hit-rate and reduce cold-start token cost by ~22%.
cesar (runtime): discovered one edge regression: prefix normalization trimmed certain control tokens which changed key semantics for a small client set -> caused cache misses and user regressions. we should maintain an allowlist of routes that bypass truncation.
anh (prod-eng): action items: 1) run canary with limited concurrency (maria) 2) deploy autoscaler hook + rate limiter (cesar) 3) add deploy-time `seed` hook to deploy bot (anh) 4) add route allowlist for truncation exceptions (maria) 5) alert + rollback policy (kevin).
maria (ml-infra): I'll start the canary now and post metrics in #eng-runtime-observability in 2 hours. will also include query sample diffs for the truncation allowlist. :eyes:
kevin (sre): +1. if we see the kernel-v2 contention persist, fallback to kernel-v1 for warmers only. low risk and easy toggle. :thumbsup:
cesar (runtime): noted. I'll add a kernel tag to warmers so we can force `kernel: v1` for preseeder traffic.
maria (ml-infra): cool — kicking off canary. ping me if you see any abnormal deploy-bot activity.
deploy-bot: canary rollout `preseeder-v1` at 10% initiated by maria. monitor: /deploys/17745
